title: Editor forgets custom theme settings on version upgrade
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.6.1.stable
- Not reproducible in: 4.5.stable

### System information

Manjaro Linux amd64, Godot v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e], no sandboxing

### Issue description

Normally Godot remembers custom editor colour theme settings when upgrading to a new minor version.

When going from 4.5 to 4.6.1, however, it seems to forget, or force-reset them. I had 4.5 set to a "custom" interface theme/colour preset, with custom base and accent colours, and theme contrast. Upon launching 4.6.1 for the first time, the editor changed my colour preset to "black", _and_ reset all the custom values to default.

Even as the UI theme is changed to a new default, I would expect the colour, contrast, etc. settings to remain the same for existing users, especially when we've modified any of them.

On another note, I think existing users shouldn't have to tinker with settings in order to keep the behaviour they're used to, so when importing settings from a previous version, base theme (classic) should also be preserved, but that may or may not be a separate issue.

### Steps to reproduce

- Make sure there are no 4.6+ editor settings files
- In 4.5 or earlier, set custom editor theme colours (base, accent, contrast), and optionally other theme settings
- Launch 4.6(.1) and check editor theme settings
